title: 2026-01-12 - Redwood All-Hands: Q1 Kickoff
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on Q1 priorities: product roadmaps for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings, reliability and infra investments, go-to-market cadence, hiring goals, and key operational metrics. Leadership covered ramp plan for Dedicated capacity, privacy/compliance milestones, and a company-wide initiative on cost/perf optimizations via Redwood Optimize. Ended with Q&A and explicit next steps for decks, hiring, and security docs.
topics: Q1 product priorities (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
Redwood Optimize launch and cost/perf initiatives
next_steps: Eli to share Q1 priorities slide deck by 2026-01-14
Jared to publish infra road map and outage playbook link by 2026-01-19
People team to open hiring ladders and interview slates for infra and SE by 2026-01-20
Product to share Redwood Optimize pilot signup form and docs
Security to circulate SOC 2 status and KMS integration notes
action_items: Eli Collins - Share Q1 priorities deck (due 2026-01-14)
Jared Kim - Publish infra runbook and downtime playbook (due 2026-01-19)
Devon Lee - Start Dedicated capacity benchmark tests and share results (due 2026-01-28)
Sofia Ramirez - Send Redwood Optimize pilot signup and evaluation criteria (due 2026-01-18)
People Team - Post hiring reqs for 4 infra and 2 SE roles (due 2026-01-20)
Security - Share SOC 2 timeline and KMS/HSM integration doc (due 2026-01-21)
transcript:
[00:00] Eli Collins: Good morning everyone, welcome to the Q1 kickoff all-hands. Um we wanted to cover the high level priorities, uh quick updates from leadership and then go to Q&A. So we got about 55 minutes.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Quick housekeeping, recording is on, slides are at drive.redwood.internal/Q1-kickoff, we'll try to keep to time.
[01:12] Jared Kim: Hey team 	6 infra update, we've been focusing on Dedicated capacity stability, we've pushed kernel fixes for memory spikes on A100s, and the KV cache eviction bug appears fixed in canary. note: sometimes gen svc reads as KV cash in logs.
[02:05] Chris O'Neal: Right, we saw a few regressions end of December around prefix caching and some OOMs; we've added extra telemetry, rolling restarts and a mitigation that reduces tail latency by about 25% in our staging runs.
[03:10] Devon Lee: Benchmarks for Dedicated vs hosted: median p95 numbers show Dedicated offering ~15-20% better p95 under heavy batching for chat workloads; latency vs cost tradeoffs still roadmap item. We'll publish a spreadsheet link after the meeting.
[04:05] Eli Collins: Thanks. On product, Sofia?
[04:18] Sofia Ramirez: Product priorities for Q1: 1) Improve model routing policies 	6 smarter fallback when capacity constrained, 2) Redwood Optimize GA: guide customers on batching, cache, and quantization profiles, 3) Private deployment improvements: easier on-prem installs and clearer KMS/HSM integrations. We'll demo some of this in the February tech deep dive.
[05:30] Lena Zhou: On rollouts 	6 canary release tooling is being expanded so teams can do A/B on model variants and automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants. There was a typo in the deck where 'Redhood' was written instead of Redwood, so ignore that slide.
[06:45] Priya Nair: GTM: We're seeing inbound interest from mid-market SaaS teams and a few enterprise pilots. Pipeline is healthy; target this quarter is 3 Dedicated contracts and 2 Private pilots. We'll be leaning on solutions for compliance-heavy verticals.
[08:00] Eli Collins: Quick note on pricing transparency: send questions to finance@redwood, we'll share the pricing rubric.
[08:30] Audience (Jessica from Sales): Quick Q 	6 for Dedicated, what's the expected SLA for p95 latency?
[08:45] Jared Kim: We're targeting SLA tiers that match enterprise needs 	6 99.9 uptime and p95 targets aligned with the hardware profile; exact numbers depend on the cluster flavor, we'll publish per-region numbers in the infra roadmap.
[09:40] Audience (Marcus, Eng): Any updates on private deployment network requirements 	6 VPC and on-prem?
[09:55] Chris O'Neal: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package for air-gapped installs. KMS integrations are in progress, we've got HSM options planned. The security team will circulate a checklist.
[11:10] Eli Collins: Security, got anything to share?
[11:20] Security (Alyssa): SOC 2 readiness: documentation is 80% complete, control mapping and third party attestations in flight; target date Q1 end for report initiation. Also SSO/SAML flows and RBAC improvements are being tracked.
[12:05] Eli Collins: Awesome. On costs: Redwood Optimize is aimed at reducing per token spend by recommending batching, caching and quant profiles per workload. Sofia?
[12:30] Sofia Ramirez: We ran internal pilots; median cost reduction 20% for retrieval-heavy apps via prefix caching and quantized model variants. The product will recommend config changes and expose estimated dollars saved. We'll pilot with 10 customers first.
[13:45] Audience (Tammy, Solutions): Are there concerns about output quality when quantizing?
[14:00] Jared Kim: Yes quality regressions are a risk; Optimize ties into evals and prompt sets to detect regressions and suggest rollback. We'll integrate with our model catalog so customers can see verified profiles.
[15:20] Eli Collins: Hiring 	6 People team?
[15:35] People (Rina): Hiring goals: 4 infra engineers, 2 production SEs, 1 product PM. Interview slates open this week. Benefits update: improved parental leave and refreshed remote stipend.
[17:00] Audience (Q general): Leadership asked for clarity on OKRs and how teams map to Q1 objectives.
[17:25] Eli Collins: We'll share the org-level OKRs document after this meeting and leaders will cascade team-level goals.
[18:10] Maya Patel: On revenue ops 	6 we're simplifying the trial to paid conversion funnel with better observability on onboarding metrics and trial usage nudges.
[19:30] Priya Nair: Partner channel 	6 two prospective cloud partners signed NDAs, exploring marketplace listing.
[20:40] Audience (Dev): Any scheduled maintenance windows for Dedicated?
[21:00] Chris O'Neal: We'll keep rolling upgrades in off-peak windows; customers with strict SLAs can opt in for managed maintenance or a freeze window.
[22:15] Eli Collins: Quick product demo tease 	6 in the slide deck there's a gut check of the new routing UI and per-route dashboards.
[23:05] Lena Zhou: The console will get per-route traces, token-level cost breakdowns and a regression alert tied to eval prompt sets. That's coming in Beta in mid Q1.
[24:40] Audience (Anna, Eng): Are we investing in custom kernels for the new Transformer variants?
[24:55] Jared Kim: Yes, kernel selection is part of the runtime; we pick optimal kernels and compilation paths by model arch and seq length distributions. We also support quant-friendly code paths.
[26:10] Eli Collins: Let's move to risks: what keeps you up at night?
[26:25] Devon Lee: Capacity and cloud spot market volatility; we need better burst policies and graceful fallback to smaller variants.
[27:05] Chris O'Neal: Also supply chain for GPUs and long lead times for hardware. We're investing in multi-cloud capacity and smarter routing to mitigate.
[28:30] Audience (Sam, Customer Success): How are we supporting customers worried about data residency?
[28:45] Security (Alyssa): We have region pinning, audit logs, and Private deployments for strict residency; KMS/HSM controls will be advertised in our compliance pack.
[30:00] Eli Collins: Quick callout 	6 internal hackweek this quarter focused on cost/perf tooling, signups are open.
[31:10] Audience (Maya): A quick ask: leaders, please be explicit about dependencies in your team planning.
[31:30] Eli Collins: Agreed. Ok Q&A lightning round 	6 please keep questions short.
[33:00] Audience (Multiple): questions on pricing, pilot timelines, partner onboarding, demo availability.
[36:20] Sofia Ramirez: We'll open Redwood Optimize pilot signups this week, limited to 10 pilots, sign up via the short form in the deck.
[38:10] Priya Nair: For Dedicated sales, solutions will package a quickstart Pilot + benchmark run for customers, includes a performance baseline and cost projection.
[40:05] Eli Collins: I'll summarize: share the Q1 deck, infra will publish roadmap and runbooks, people will start hiring, security to share SOC2/KMS docs.
[41:20] Audience (Kim): Will there be follow-up town halls per region?
[41:35] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll do smaller region-specific sessions and a technical deep dive in Feb.
[42:05] Audience (Jon): Any changes to comp or target for sales?
[42:20] Priya Nair: Compensation plans are separate, we'll update SDR/AE targets after a final review next week.
[43:10] Eli Collins: Closing notes 	6 thanks team, energize for a busy quarter. One ask: be vocal if you see customer pain points.
[44:00] Audience (applause):
[44:30] Eli Collins: Ok, that's it. We'll post recording and slides. Action items captured in the meeting notes.
[45:00] Moderator: Meeting end recording stop.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (mis-heard product names, punctuation and run-ons). References to outside docs: drive.redwood.internal/Q1-kickoff, infra/redwood/roadmap, optimize/pilot-signup (links internal).
